record.paper_title: Developments and open problems on chiral polytopes
record.original_question: Determine the pairs of positive integers (m, n) for which there exists a chiral 4-polytope whose right Petrie paths have length m and whose left Petrie paths have length n.

evidence.quote: Problem 11 Determine the pairs (m, n) for which there exists a chiral 4-polytope with right Petrie paths of length m and left Petrie paths of length n.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
An abstract polytope of rank $n$ is a partially ordered set $\mathcal{P}$ (with elements called faces, ranked from $-1$ to $n$) satisfying the standard axioms: it has a unique minimum face $F_{-1}$ and unique maximum face $F_n$; every maximal chain (flag) contains exactly $n+2$ faces; $\mathcal{P}$ is strongly flag-connected; and it satisfies the diamond condition (whenever $F<G$ with $\mathrm{rank}(G)-\mathrm{rank}(F)=2$, there are exactly two faces strictly between $F$ and $G$).

The automorphism group $\Gamma(\mathcal{P})$ acts freely on the set of flags. The polytope $\mathcal{P}$ is called chiral if $\Gamma(\mathcal{P})$ has exactly two orbits on the flags, and adjacent flags (differing in exactly one face) lie in distinct orbits. For a chiral polytope, fix a base flag $\Phi=\{F_{-1},F_0,\dots,F_n\}$; then there exist generators $\sigma_1,\dots,\sigma_{n-1}$ of $\Gamma(\mathcal{P})$, where $\sigma_i$ fixes all faces of $\Phi$ except $F_{i-1}$ and $F_i$ and cyclically permutes consecutive $i$-faces in the section $F_{i+1}/F_{i-2}$.

For a chiral $4$-polytope, define the right Petrie element $\rho_R = \sigma_1\sigma_2\sigma_3$ and the left Petrie element $\rho_L = \sigma_1\sigma_2^{-1}\sigma_3$. The orbits of edges (or equivalently, the closed zig-zag paths through the $1$-skeleton that turn alternately right/left at successive faces) under $\langle\rho_R\rangle$ and $\langle\rho_L\rangle$ are called the right Petrie paths and left Petrie paths, and their common lengths are the orders of $\rho_R$ and $\rho_L$ respectively.

Determine all pairs $(m,n)$ of positive integers for which there exists a chiral $4$-polytope whose right Petrie paths have length $m$ and whose left Petrie paths have length $n$.

The problem appears to remain open.
